solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vulgar young person losing head confronts superior officer — big trouble

indicators.note: confronts means stands facing, so the shortened youth comes first, face to face with the officer
losing its head means the first letter of the word for the youth is dropped

parts.note: a chav is British slang for a brash, loutish youth
OC is short for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: A loutish youth squares up to his commanding officer, and serious trouble follows.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAV, British slang for a brash lout, loses its head C to leave HAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread chaos and destruction, a case of very big trouble.

clue.text: Control the situation before laying down requirements for others at the table?

definitions.text: Control the situation before laying down requirements for others at the table?

parts.words: Control the situation before laying down requirements for others at the table?
parts.note: the idiom for being in total control, pictured as a card player keeping every card before the deal is laid out

explanation.surface: A dealer controls the game before laying out what others at the table need.
explanation.definitionFit: To have every advantage is the idiom's meaning: control of the situation.

clue.text: Guarantee given with very little indication of pain

parts.note: ouch is a short cry showing pain

explanation.surface: A promise made with barely a wince.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouch for something is to guarantee it.

clue.text: A linguistic sign from the Man in Black?

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Cilla Black was a British singer and TV presenter
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: A sign of some kind given by a mysterious figure dressed in black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man in Black' suggests Johnny Cash; Black is Cilla Black, a British singer and TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is the mark under a c, as in French, showing a soft sound: a linguistic sign.

clue.text: Musicians turn out to be inadequate dilettanti

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word for turn out is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to come out is to turn out, as in 'it came out well'
dilettanti are amateurs who pose as experts, poseurs or posers

explanation.surface: A sneer that so-called musicians prove to be mere amateurs.
explanation.walkthrough: COME (turn out) is inadequate, losing its end to give COM.
explanation.definitionFit: Composers write music, so they are musicians of a creative kind.

clue.text: College student humoured, though denied a sign of affection

indicators.note: denied means deprived of, so letters are taken away

parts.note: to coax is to humour or persuade gently
X is a kiss

explanation.surface: A student was indulged but not given a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: COAXED loses A and X (a kiss).
explanation.definitionFit: A co-ed is a female student at a mixed college, chiefly American usage.

clue.text: Stinky meal prepared incorrectly

indicators.note: prepared as in a dish being made up, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A smelly dinner that has been badly cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something mistakenly means doing it in error, incorrectly.

clue.text: Unfashionable model gets to survive

parts.note: out means out of fashion
a last is a shoemaker's model of a foot

explanation.surface: An out-of-date fashion model is still managing to hang on.
explanation.walkthrough: A cobbler's last is the foot-shaped block shoes are built on.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast is to live or last longer than others, to survive.

clue.text: Train journey going on time — Euston evacuated earlier

indicators.note: earlier means the emptied station goes before the rest
evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters of the station's name remain

parts.note: a tour is a journey
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A train trip running on schedule, after an empty Euston station.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston is a London railway terminus; 'evacuated' leaves EN. 'Train' is not a railway train but a retinue.
explanation.definitionFit: A train of followers, as in a royal train, is a retinue or entourage.

clue.text: Commentators finally interpret a man's rambling, not completely clear

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word is taken
rambling means wandering, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Pundits end up decoding a man's rambling, which is far from clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only partly see-through is not completely clear.

clue.text: The French female has to get ready for bed — she's washing

parts.note: la is the French feminine form of 'the'
to undress is to take off clothes before bed

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman has to get ready for bed while doing the laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman whose job is washing clothes and linen.

clue.text: Symbol put back by weather forecasters with books

indicators.note: put back means the letters are set down in reverse order

parts.note: the Met Office is the British weather service, the Met for short
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Weather forecasters shelve a symbol back among their books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses MET + OT; the Met is the UK's weather forecasting office.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem that serves as the symbol of a clan or group.

clue.text: A cold island off the Irish coast

parts.note: a chill is a cold, or coldness

explanation.surface: A cold, windswept island lies off Ireland's coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Achill is a large island off County Mayo in western Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Achill is the largest island off the coast of Ireland, in County Mayo.

clue.text: Primitive weapon has a gentle hit stopping movement

indicators.note: stopping is used as filling a gap, so one piece plugs the middle of another

parts.note: a cult is a movement, a fashion or following
a tap is a light blow

explanation.surface: An ancient siege weapon is said to land a soft blow that halts all motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' means plugging a gap, not halting; 'movement' is a following, not motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult is an early siege engine for hurling stones, a weapon of primitive design.

clue.text: Grumble when church is seen as one being smug

indicators.note: is seen as means one thing appears in place of another, a swap

parts.note: a complaint is a grumble
I is the Roman numeral for one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Grumbling when church is treated as one is a self-satisfied gripe.
explanation.walkthrough: In COMPLAINT, the I (one) is replaced by CE (Church of England).
explanation.definitionFit: A complacent person is self-satisfied, smug.

clue.text: Faithful old individual grabbing paper is granted solitude

indicators.note: grabbing means holding onto, so the newspaper is clutched within the old word for faithful

parts.note: leal is an archaic and Scottish word for loyal or faithful
FT is the Financial Times newspaper
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A loyal old soul grabs the paper and is at last given some peace.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAL is old or Scots for loyal; the FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: To be not disturbed by anyone is to be granted solitude.

clue.text: Dynamism, as befits marines giving warning of danger

parts.note: fire is energy, dynamism
à la means in the manner of, as befits
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Energy fit for the marines when they are sounding the alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire alarm is a bell or siren warning of danger from fire.

clue.text: Joyful bit of song from central Africa

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A cheerful snatch of song heard in central Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' picks the letters out of cenTRAL Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tra-la is a nonsense refrain sung in a carefree, happy way.

clue.text: Female group run by male

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: A group of women is run by a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women of a household, a female group, especially wives of one man.

clue.text: Officer damages room, scratching floor

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: scratching the floor means removing the bottom letter of the room, this being a down entry

parts.note: a hall is a room

explanation.surface: An officer trashes a room and scrapes up the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the floor is the last letter, so HALL loses its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshal is a high-ranking officer, as in field marshal.

clue.text: Robbers having similar drinks outside and inside?

indicators.note: outside means one drink wraps round the other

parts.note: pils is pilsner, a pale beer
lager is a similar drink, the pale beer of which pils is one kind

explanation.surface: Thieves drinking the same thing both before and after a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'similar' is there because both drinks are pale beers: pils is pilsner, a kind of lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillagers are plunderers who rob with violence, especially in war.

clue.text: Hypersensitivity of friend without some measure of work

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the friend goes round the unit

parts.note: an ally is a friend
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: An allergy to the effort of a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is the body's oversensitive reaction to a substance.

clue.text: Boss to carry player on a lap of honour?

definitions.meaning: the boss of a board or meeting, the person in charge

definitions.text: to carry player on a lap of honour?
definitions.meaning: to chair a man is to carry a player shoulder-high round the ground

explanation.surface: A boss is asked to carry a victorious player round the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, chair (carry shoulder-high) plus man (player).
explanation.definitionFit: The chairman of a company or meeting is its head, the boss.

clue.text: I may be put out by outrageous leading lady

indicators.note: outrageous means wild, so the remaining letters are rearranged
put out means removed, so the I is dropped from the following word

explanation.surface: An actor says she may be thrown out by a scandalous leading lady.
explanation.walkthrough: LEADING without its I leaves LEADNG, which 'outrageous' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenda is a woman's name, and crosswords often define a given name as just a lady.

clue.text: Wild animal in article about place to the north

indicators.note: to the north means going upwards, so in a down entry the letters run backwards
about means surrounding, so the article goes round the verb

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to lay is to place

explanation.surface: A wild beast in an article about some northern spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the article round the verb; 'to the north' then turns the result upward, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned African antelope, a wild animal.

clue.text: Cold caught in the course of school hospital examination

indicators.note: caught in the course of means held within, so one letter sits inside the other

parts.note: a san is a sanatorium, the sickbay of a British boarding school

explanation.surface: A cold picked up at school leads to a hospital check.
explanation.walkthrough: SAN is the school sanatorium, the sickbay of a British boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A scan is a medical examination by imaging.

clue.text: Spread the gospel but not quietly to gain influence

indicators.note: but not means without, so a letter is taken away from the word for evangelising

parts.note: to preach is to spread the gospel
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Evangelise, but quietly, so as to win people over.
explanation.walkthrough: PREACH drops P (piano, quietly).
explanation.definitionFit: Reach as a noun is one's range of power or sway, that is, influence.

clue.text: Savage old lover appearing with naughty erotica

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are set in a disordered way

explanation.surface: A former partner turns up with saucy erotica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savage' is a verb here, to attack verbally, not an adjective about the lover; 'naughty' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To savage critics' style is to excoriate: to attack fiercely in words.

clue.text: Is backward-looking politician exposed as a fool?

indicators.note: backward-looking means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
to let on is to reveal, to expose a secret

explanation.surface: Is the reactionary politician being shown up as an idiot?
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward-looking' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish or gullible person.

clue.text: For riser, inactivity's ending — whence comes the dawn?

indicators.note: ending means the last letter is taken

parts.note: the sun rises in the east

explanation.surface: For an early riser, idleness ends where daylight breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is a raising agent that makes dough rise, so in bread it is the riser.
